title: Contract
description: Root of the generated wire contract schema.

Account.description: A connected provider account. Its token is kept in the vault, under its id.

credential.description:
Another account whose saved sign-in this one shares: one provider sign-in
can cover several workspaces, and its refresh token works only once,
so they keep one copy. Null when the account holds its own.

external_id.description: The provider's id for the account, team or organization.

in_1password.description: The token lives in 1Password: Hoista keeps only its `op://` reference.

last_discovery.description: How the last look for its resources went; null before the first.

scopes.description: What the token was checked to be allowed to do, when connected.

AccountChoice.description: An account a token can reach, offered for the person to choose. Not connected yet.

external_id.description: Provider account ID or organization slug consumed by the adapter.

name.description: Its name at the provider, checked before it's shown.

AccountDiagnostic.description: One account's check result. Holds no tokens, provider responses or connection strings.

checked_at.description:
RFC 3339 time the check finished; null when it didn't run or the account is
disconnected.

message.description: What to do next. Never the provider's own error text.

status.description: Result of this check; the saved account status is not changed.

verified_scopes.description: Permissions the check saw; not a full list of what the token can write.

AccountDiagnosticStatus.description: Result of checking an account. Passing doesn't prove every write permission.

oneOf.description: The token check and read checks passed.
No saved credential exists.
The provider refused the token as expired or revoked.
The provider refused a permission the check needs.
The keychain, the adapter or the network couldn't finish the check.
This account's check timed out; whether the token works is unknown.
The account is disconnected; no token was read.
Not checked: the overall time ran out, or the account changed during the check.

AccountStatus.description: Whether a connected account's token works.

oneOf.description: The token works.
The provider no longer accepts the token.
The token lacks permissions Hoista needs.
No usable token: the person disconnected it, or it came from a backup.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for older events; null on the last page.

Agent.description: An agent the person let connect, and what it may do.

grant.description:
What it may touch beyond its scopes: which projects and environments,
tools it may never use, and when the grant ends.

last_seen.description: When it last did anything (RFC 3339, UTC).

revoked.description: Whether the person cut it off.

AgentException.description:
One exception: a group of resources (in every project, or one) or a
single resource, and how far it narrows access there.

group.description: A group of resources; set this or `resource_id`.

project_id.description:
With a group: the project it applies in, or null for every project.
With a resource: the project it's in, for showing it.

AgentGrant.description:
Where an agent's scopes apply. Deny wins: a tool in `deny` is refused
whatever the scopes say; a project outside `projects` is refused for every tool.

deny.description: Tool names it may never call, whatever its scopes.

environment_ids.description:
Hoista environment ids whose projects it may touch; null means every
environment, including new ones.

environment_rules.description:
Stricter rules by Hoista environment id: what it may do to projects
in that environment, on top of its access.

exceptions.description:
Narrower access for some resources, on top of everything above. An
exception only ever narrows; the strictest one that applies wins.

expires_at.description:
RFC 3339 UTC end of the grant; null means no end date (inactivity
expiry still applies).

projects.description: Project ids it may touch; null means every project, including new ones.

version.description: Raised on every change, so a decision can name the policy it used.

without_asking.description:
Full access: what would need the person's OK (deleting or removing
anything, connecting an account) goes ahead without
asking. Off for "Ask for approval": Hoista asks in the agent first.

AgentTransport.description: How an agent reaches the engine.

oneOf.description: A coding tool on this computer, over stdio.
A chat app or cloud agent, connected with OAuth.

Approval.description: A request for the person's approval, for one action on one thing. It lapses after 15 minutes.

deletion.description: For a delete, everything it would remove.

reason.description: The agent's reason, shown to the person.

target.description: What it wants to do it to: a resource, or a hash of the exact operation.

ApprovalDecision.description: Where a request for the person's approval stands. An approval is used once.

oneOf.description: Waiting for the person.
The person allowed it; not used yet.
The person declined it.
Not decided before it expired.
Allowed and used; it can't be used again.

ApprovalDisplay.description: Desktop projection preserving terminal states and exact deletion confirmation material.

action.description: Exact server-side action this request authorizes.

agent_detail.description: Execution semantics shown alongside the agent identity.

agent_name.description: Registered display name, or identity when unavailable.

allow_blocked.description: Reason Desktop cannot offer Allow; decline remains possible.

confirm_text.description: Exact name the UI requires before permitting Allow.

confirmation.description: Saved deletion fingerprint and backup policy for the decision request.

decision.description: Null for pending; otherwise allow, decline, expired or consumed.

details.description: Exact before/after settings for non-resource changes.

id.description: Approval identity used for the decision request.

if_allowed.description: Scope and execution behavior after permission is granted.

reason.description: Original request explanation, rendered as text.

ApprovalDisplayDetail.description: One exact setting shown in a non-resource approval review.

value.description: The value as saved when the approval was asked for.

ApprovalDisplayTarget.description: Display-only resource target; operations without resources have an empty target list.

label.description: Kind of effect, such as deletion or disruption.

name.description: Display name from Hoista's own records, not from the agent.

AttentionFeed.description: Two lists, each paged on its own. Follow both cursors to read the whole feed.

approvals.description: Pending approvals from this approval page.

next_cursor.description: Approvals cursor, even when the filtered page is empty.

notices.description: Notices for this page of projects; they don't claim savings or current health.

project_next_cursor.description: Project scan cursor, even for pages without notices.

AttentionNotice.description: An issue or suggestion. Reading it changes nothing at any provider.

oneOf.description: The newest deployment attempt failed; live resources may still be healthy.
A resource's provider reports it failing (a crashed or failed deployment).
A resource that serves requests got none on every day checked; worth a look.

days.description: Number of full days with usage reported.

resource_id.description: Resource to review; this is not permission to pause it.

AttentionQuery.description: Separate cursors for the approvals list and the project scan.

project_cursor.description: Project scan cursor. An empty page can still have one.

Backup.description:
Everything a backup holds. Restored resources always start out watched,
not managed.

accounts.description: Connected accounts, without their tokens. Each one is reconnected after a restore.

custom_domains.description: Custom domains and the resources they point at.

links.description: The links between resources on the project map.

projects.description: Projects and where their source is.

BindingRefresh.description:
What one binding refresh covered. A binding that can't be matched to one
resource is left alone, never guessed.

relationships_complete.description: Always false: bindings aren't every possible dependency.

resolved.description: Bindings resolved to resources in a project, on the same account.

resource_id.description: The resource whose bindings were read.

unresolved.description: Bindings left unknown: unsupported, pointing outside a project, missing or ambiguous.

Capabilities.description:
Everything an adapter can do. Clients and agents read these to decide what
to show and offer; nothing checks a provider by name.

bills.description: Reports what the provider has billed so far this period.

browser_sign_in.description: Connects by signing in on the provider's own page, instead of a pasted token.

containers.description:
Runs what Hoista deploys as a long-running container built from the
project's Dockerfile, which Hoista writes for a Node project without one.

cron.description: Runs a deployed web or job resource on exact UTC cron schedules.

delete.description:
Deletes a resource at the provider (a provider project, service, Worker, bucket or
domain), when the person confirms it by name.

discover.description: Lists existing resources in the account.

dns_zones.description: Creates the DNS zone for a domain it adds, when asked to.

new_bucket.description: Creates an object storage bucket at the provider.

new_database.description:
Creates a database of its own at the provider (a Postgres project, or a
database next to a project's services).

new_email_domain.description: Adds a domain to send email from.

new_from_folder.description:
Creates a new project at the provider from a folder on this computer,
with the provider's own command-line tool.

new_from_image.description: Runs a container image as a new resource (a service, or a GPU pod).

new_project.description: Creates a new project at the provider from a repository.

plan_deploy.description:
Hoista builds a project folder and deploys it here from a plan
(`plan_deploy`).

project_database.description: Where Hoista creates a project's Postgres when its plan needs one.

provider_deploys.description:
Lists the provider's deployments of a watched resource, and redeploys or
rolls back through the provider's own actions.

provider_details.description:
Reads a watched resource's settings, deployments and addresses as the
provider keeps them (the provider tab).

provider_operations.description: Runs the provider's own API operations by name (see `provider_operations`).

provider_variables.description: Reads and changes a watched resource's variables at the provider.

rollback.description: Rolls back to an earlier release.

server.description: Can run Hoista itself as a remote, from the published image.

upload.description: Uploads a folder for the provider to build and deploy.

CheckStatus.description: A health check result distinguishes unavailable functionality from healthy checks.

oneOf.description: The check succeeded.
The user must take action.
Not yet implemented or deliberately not checked.

CustomDomain.description: A custom domain and the resource it points at.

hostname.description: The domain, in lowercase ASCII, without `https://` or a path.

observed.description: What the provider last said about it.

resource_id.description: The resource that answers on it.

DaemonStatus.description: Identity and restart state of a running daemon, separate from general readiness.

instance_id.description: Random process instance identity used to reject stale restart requests.

mcp_command.description:
The exact command a coding tool runs to reach this daemon over MCP:
the `hoist` binary beside this daemon, its state folder when it is not
the default one, then `mcp`. Empty when the binary can't be found.

pid.description: Current process ID, for diagnostics only.

restart_requested.description: An owner restart has been accepted; completion still requires a new instance.

supervised.description: Launched in service-manager mode; the manager is responsible for replacement after exit.

DailyTraffic.description: One UTC day in the overview chart.

errors.description: Sum across the same resources, or null when unavailable.

requests.description: Sum across request-serving resources, or null when coverage is incomplete.

DatabaseArchive.description:
A finished, checked copy of a database (`pg_dump`'s custom format), saved
where only this user can read it.

branch_id.description: The provider's branch the database is on.

path.description: Where the file is on this computer. It holds the app's data, so treat it like the database.

resource_id.description: The database resource it was taken from.

is_default.description: Whether the provider marks it as the default branch.

logical_size_bytes.description: How much data it holds, in bytes. Not what's billed for storage.

parent_id.description: The branch it was made from, which may since have been deleted.

state.description: The provider's word for its state. Whether it's running is on the compute.

DatabaseCompute.description: One compute: the server a branch runs on.

kind.description: The provider's kind, such as `read_write` or `read_only`.

max_compute_units.description: The most compute units it's set to use. A setting, not a measurement.

min_compute_units.description: The fewest compute units it's set to use. A setting, not a measurement.

pending_state.description: The state it's changing to, while it changes.

state.description: Its state. `idle` means asleep, not broken.

suspend_timeout_seconds.description:
How long it waits idle before sleeping, in seconds. `0` is the
provider's default; `-1` means it never sleeps.

DatabaseIdentity.description: Which database a resource is, at its provider.

database_name.description: The database's name on that branch.

owner_name.description: The role that owns it, which Hoista connects as to make a copy.

DatabaseObservation.description:
A database's branches and computes. They come from two separate calls, so
one can be a moment newer than the other.

branches.description: The branches that exist now. Deleted ones are left out.

wake_count.description: How many times it woke up, when the provider reports it.

DatabaseOperation.description:
One thing the provider did to the database, such as starting or suspending
a compute. No error text or connection details.

action.description: What was done, in the provider's words, such as `start_compute`.

branch_id.description: The branch, which may no longer exist.

compute_id.description: The compute, which may no longer exist.

id.description: The provider's id. The same one can come back on the next page.

status.description: How it went. `failed` can still be retried by the provider.

updated_at.description: When it last changed, which isn't necessarily when it finished.

DatabaseOperationHistory.description:
One page of a database's operations. Providers only keep so much history,
so pages never add up to a complete record.

complete_history.description: Always `false`: this is never the whole history.

completed_starts_in_page.description: How many computes finished starting on this page alone.

next_cursor.description: Pass this to get the next page. `null` means the provider gave no next page.

DatabaseTarget.description: A database a delete would remove, with the resource it belongs to.

DeletionConfirmation.description: The person's confirmation, for exactly the preview they saw.

backup_databases.description:
Copy the databases before deleting. On unless the person turns it off,
which only they can, and only when deleting a whole project.

confirmation_name.description: The name they typed, exactly as shown.

DeletionDomain.description:
A custom domain that would stop pointing at the deleted resource. The
domain itself and its DNS zone stay.

resource_id.description: The resource it points at now.

zone_id.description: Its DNS zone at the provider, to check the domain is still the person's.

DeletionPreview.description:
Everything Hoista knows a delete would affect. It covers what Hoista has
recorded, not everything in the provider account.

affected_resources.description: Resources that stay but depend on something being deleted.

blockers.description: Why it can't be deleted right now. None doesn't mean the data is saved anywhere.

confirmation_name.description: The name the person types to confirm.

database_export_available.description: Whether this build of Hoista can copy a database before deleting it.

databases.description: Every database on each database resource being deleted.

domains.description: Custom domains that stop pointing anywhere. The domains themselves stay.

fingerprint.description: A hash of all of the above. The delete is refused if anything has changed since.

latest_deploy_id.description: The newest deploy when this was shown. A newer deploy means showing it again.

links.description: The map links that touch what's being deleted, including ones marked missing.

resources.description: What gets deleted, in the order it will be: databases last.

target.description: The project or resource being deleted.

DeletionResource.description: A resource at a provider that the delete would touch.

kind.description: What it is. A database's data is gone for good unless it's copied first.

project_id.description: Its project, which can be another project when the resource is shared.

provider_ref.description: What the provider calls it: exactly what will be deleted there.

url.description: Its public address, so the person sees what stops answering.

DeliveryState.description: Where one event's delivery to one webhook stands.

oneOf.description: Waiting for its next try.
The receiver answered 2xx.
Gave up after six tries; kept as history.

Deploy.description: One deploy or rollback, kept in the project's history whether it worked or not.

cancel_requested.description: Whether the person stopped it. It stops at the next point where stopping is safe.

channel.description: Which app it was asked for from.

duration_ms.description: How long it took, in milliseconds.

environment_keys.description: The variables given for this deploy only, by name. Their values are never saved.

failure.description: Why it failed; null when it didn't, or Hoista stopped before it could tell.

provenance.description: What the source copy held; null when copying didn't finish.

release_version.description: The project's release number (v1, v2, …); null until it's live, and for failed deploys.

releases.description: What it released at each provider, to roll back to later.

rollback_of.description: For a rollback, the deploy it went back to.

source_observation.description:
A first look at the source before it was copied; null while queued, or
when it stopped before looking.

started_by.description: The person, or the agent's id.

started_by_name.description: The agent's name when it asked, so renaming it later doesn't rewrite history.

title.description: What the change is, in the person's words. Never taken from a commit message.

url.description: The address it was checked to answer on.

version.description: Counts up with each deploy of the project, failed ones included.

DeployChannel.description: Which app a deploy was asked for from. Who asked is recorded separately.

oneOf.description: Hoista Desktop.
The `hoist` command line.
An agent, over MCP.

DeployFailure.description: Why a deploy failed, as far as Hoista knows.

compensation_failed.description: Whether undoing the partial release failed. `false` doesn't prove it was all undone.

message.description: What went wrong, in plain words, with secrets taken out.

missing_secrets.description: Variables the project needs that weren't set. Names only.

provider_response.description: The provider's last failed answer, when the failure was one.

release_started.description: Whether it had started releasing, so something may have changed at the provider.

steps.description: The steps running when it failed; empty when it failed before starting.

DeployOptions.description: Options for a deploy or a rollback. A rollback refuses `expected_plan_revision`.

channel.description: Which app asked. An agent's deploys are always recorded as MCP.

expected_plan_revision.description: The plan revision the person looked at; refused if the plan has changed. Without it, the current plan is used.

request_key.description:
A UUID that makes it safe to retry: sending the same key again returns
the first attempt. A deploy with a key must also give `expected_plan_revision`.

title.description: What the change is, in the person's words: 1 to 160 characters.

oneOf.description: Accepted and waiting to start.
Building or releasing.
Released and serving.
Stopped with an error.
Replaced by a rollback to an earlier deployment.

DeployStep.description: Progress through one step of a deployment.

message.description: What happened, with secrets taken out.

DeploymentRequest.description: A deploy request found by its key.

deploy_id.description: The deploy it started, kept even if that deploy's history was deleted.

deployment.description:
The deploy as it stands now, or null if its history was deleted. Null
still means the request was accepted.

project_id.description: The project, kept even if the project has since been deleted.

request_key.description: The key, as a lowercase UUID. Each caller's keys are their own.

DescriptionCandidate.description: One matching resource, with its account and project so similar matches can be told apart.

account_id.description: Local account id, to tell apart resources on different accounts.

matched.description: The id, name, provider project name or hostname that matched. Not proof of a dependency.

name.description: Name as the provider shows it.

project_id.description:
The project it is in now; grouping never moves it out of another project. `app_id` is
the older name.

provider_ref.description: The provider's reference for it; part of what the review token covers.

DescriptionResolution.description: Resources matching a description. Reading it changes nothing.

ambiguous.description:
True when matches on different providers or of different kinds overlap; nothing is chosen
automatically.

candidates.description: Up to 100 candidates to review and choose from.

review_token.description: Token for exactly this result, to pass back when grouping. Grants no access.

selection_required.description: Always true: a description never groups resources without a choice.

DiagnosticAccount.description: An account as last saved. Its token isn't checked again.

DiagnosticDeploy.description: One deploy: its steps' names and statuses, never log text.

channel.description: Which app started it, without saying who.

compensation_failed.description:
Whether undoing the failed deploy failed too. `false` doesn't prove
everything was put back. Null when it didn't fail.

failure_code.description: Why it failed, as a code; any code not on Hoista's list is `unclassified`.

release_started.description: Whether the release had started when it failed; null when it didn't fail.

started_at.description: When it started (UTC); null when the saved time isn't valid.

status.description: How it ended. Says nothing about whether it's healthy now.

steps_truncated.description: Whether it had more steps than that.

DiagnosticIssue.description: A section that couldn't be read. No error text or paths.

code.description: What went wrong, as a code.

reference.description: The project, when only its deploys couldn't be read.

DiagnosticProject.description: A project and its newest deployments.

mode.description: Whether Hoista manages it or only watches it.

older_deployments_omitted.description: Whether it has older deploys than these.

reference.description: Its reference in this report. Never its name or folder.

DiagnosticReceipt.description: Where a saved report is. The path itself isn't in the report.

path.description: The saved file, for the person to look at or share.

DiagnosticReport.description:
A support report. Every id in it is hashed with a salt made for this
report alone, so it means nothing outside it.

accounts.description: Up to 100 accounts, without their names, provider ids or scopes.

accounts_truncated.description: Whether there were more accounts than that.

collection_errors.description: Sections that couldn't be read. An empty list there doesn't mean there was nothing.

engine_version.description: The version of Hoista that made it.

generated_at.description: When the report was made. Not when any provider was last checked.

limitations.description: What the report leaves out, and how to read it.

platform.description: The operating system and processor Hoista was built for.

projects.description: Up to 100 projects, each with up to its ten newest deploys.

projects_truncated.description: Whether there were more projects than that.

resources.description: Up to 100 resources, without their provider ids or addresses.

resources_truncated.description: Whether there were more resources than that.

DiagnosticResource.description: A resource as last saved, without the provider's ids.

mode.description: Whether Hoista manages it or only watches it.

project.description: Its project's reference, when it's in one.

DiagnosticStep.description: One deploy step, without its message.

name.description: Its name, or `other` for a name not on Hoista's list.

DiscoveryResult.description: What a look for an account's resources found, and what it couldn't look at.

complete.description: True only when every supported discovery family was inspected successfully.

items.description: Resources observed and saved locally without changing provider resources.

warnings.description: Inaccessible families; absence is not proof that those resources do not exist.

DiscoverySummary.description: How the last look for an account's resources went.

complete.description: Whether all supported inventory families completed successfully.

observed_at.description: Completion time of this scan attempt.

observed_resources.description: Number observed in this scan; null if it did not finish.

warnings.description: Coverage gaps or a generic failed-scan explanation.

DiscoveryWarning.description: A resource family that could not be inspected during discovery.

message.description: Safe explanation without provider response bodies.

resource_type.description: Provider resource family, such as workers or pages.

DoctorCheck.description: One diagnostic with a concrete next step where needed.

DoctorReport.description: How this Hoista is doing, and, when asked, whether each account's token still works.

accounts.description: Bounded account verification page when an engine is available.

checks.description: Individual checks, including explicitly unchecked integrations.

mode.description: daemon or direct, depending on the state owner.

DomainDnsPurpose.description: What a suggested DNS record is for.

oneOf.description: Sends visitors to the resource. A CNAME or address records, not both.
Lets the provider issue the certificate (an ACME challenge).
Proves the domain is yours. Any one of these is enough.

DomainDnsRecord.description:
A DNS record the provider suggests. Some are alternatives to each other:
one routing record is enough, not all of them.

value.description: Its value: an address, a CNAME target or TXT text, without quotes.

DomainDnsRecordType.description: The DNS record types a provider may ask for.

oneOf.description: IPv4 address.
IPv6 address.
Another name to follow.
Text, usually to prove the domain is yours.

DomainObservation.description: What the provider said about a domain, when it was added or last checked.

certificate_id.description: The provider's id for its certificate, when known.

dns.description: Whether DNS is set up, by the provider's own check.

dns_records.description: DNS records the provider suggests. Hoista shows them; it never adds them itself.

https.description: Whether the HTTPS certificate is ready. DNS can be ready before it is.

nameservers.description: The nameservers the domain has to use, as the provider says.

provider_domain_id.description: The provider's id for the domain.

registrar.description: Where the domain is registered, when the provider says. It can be out of date.

warnings.description: Anything the person should know, such as a step only they can do.

zone_id.description: The DNS zone's id at the provider. Empty when the provider doesn't run the domain's DNS.

zone_name.description: The DNS zone's name: the provider's, or the one the person chose.

DomainReadiness.description: Whether the provider says something is ready.

oneOf.description: Ready.
Waiting for DNS, or for the certificate to be issued.
Failed, or switched off.
The provider doesn't say, or couldn't be asked.

Environment.description:
A separate space for projects, such as `default` or `production`. Agents
can be limited to some of them. Nothing at the providers changes with it.

id.description: Stable id; `env_default` for the default one.

name.description: Lowercase name with letters, digits and hyphens, unique among environments.

EnvironmentChange.description: One variable to set across a project.

name.description: The variable's name. Each name once per request.

value.description: Its new value, at most 16 KiB. Held in memory that's wiped after use.

EnvironmentDeployRequest.description: Set variables across every running resource in a project, then deploy.

changes.description: 1 to 64 changes, with at most 64 KiB of values in all.

channel.description: Which app sent it. Hoista Desktop when not given.

expected_plan_revision.description:
The plan revision the person looked at. If the plan has changed since,
nothing is kept or queued.

request_key.description:
A UUID that makes the request safe to retry: sending the same key with
the same values returns the first attempt.

title.description: What the change is, in the person's words.

EnvironmentKeyRecovery.description:
A report for the person on the key, to help get it back. Holds no key,
fingerprint or hash.

active_reference.description: The keychain entry holding the key, to check or restore; null before setup.

pending_references.description: Keychain entries of setups that didn't finish, up to sixteen.

retired_attempts.description: How many unfinished setups the person retired. Their entries are kept.

retry_setup_allowed.description: Whether `--retry-setup` can be used: there are unfinished setups and no key.

review_token.description:
Pass this to `--retry-setup`, so it only acts on what this report
showed. Grants nothing on its own.

state.description: Where the key stood when checked. It can change after.

EnvironmentKeyState.description: Where the key stands, as read from the keychain just now.

oneOf.description: No key has been made yet.
The key is there and is the one recorded.
The keychain entry is gone.
The keychain entry holds something other than the key recorded.
The keychain couldn't be read, or didn't answer in time.

EnvironmentVariable.description: A variable as the apps see it: never its value, or even its fingerprint.

browser_visible.description: Whether it's built into what browsers download, so anyone can read it.

managed_by.description: The provider, when the provider sets it itself.

requires_source_sync.description: It was changed in Hoista; the project's `.env` files haven't caught up, so they mustn't overwrite it.

set_by.description: Who set it last, when known.

ErrorDto.description: Stable error body without internal causes or submitted values.

missing_secrets.description: Required environment names when known; absent in older responses.

provider_response.description: Final failed provider response metadata, if known.

recovery.description: Conservative recovery advice, when there is any.

EventDto.description: A durable server-sent event; id is encoded as text to preserve integer precision.

id.description: Where to resume from; also sent as the SSE event id.

kind.description: Stable event type, also sent in the SSE event field.

project_id.description: Project identifier when an event belongs to a project.

subject_id.description:
The record the event is about: a deployment for `deploy.*`, an approval
for `approval.*`, and likewise for agents, resources, domains and
accounts. Null when no single record applies or the event predates
this field; never parse the summary instead.

summary.description: Description with no submitted profile or credential values.

GatedAction.description: Actions an agent must have the person approve.

oneOf.description: Let an app connect as an agent, with the access it asked for.
Remove a project and its resources.
Remove one provider resource.
Remove a custom domain and its certificate. The project stays.
Connect a new provider account.

A destructive operation at a provider (delete, restore over, reset), from
the provider's operation list.

TransferAbandoned.description: A journal was abandoned without deleting potentially late credential writes.

TransferExportResult.description: Published encrypted file; durability is separate from successful publication.

bytes.description: The encrypted file's size in bytes. Small enough for JavaScript to hold exactly.

durable.description: Whether the containing directory was synchronized after publication.

next_step.description: Recovery guidance if publication succeeded but durability is uncertain.

TransferInspection.description: Authenticated transfer contents summarized without disclosing credential values.

activity_truncated.description: Whether older activity was omitted by the export cap.

ignored_resources.description: Ignored resources preserved in the transfer.

restored.description: Inspection never installs the contents; always false.

TransferRecovery.description: Recent restore attempts and explicit credential-retention behavior.

TransferRestoreRecord.description:
The keychain entries one restore made, so an abandoned restore can be
cleaned up. No tokens.

credential_references.description: The keychain entries it writes, chosen before any is written.

TransferRestoreResult.description: Completed local installation, separate from provider-access verification.

credentials_staged.description: Provider credentials written and read back locally.

mode.description: Imported projects start in watching mode.

provider_access_verified.description: False until a separate provider check succeeds.

TransferRestoreStatus.description:
Where a restore got to. Abandoned ones are kept until the person removes
them.

record.description: The restore and its keychain entries.

Usage.description: Daily resource usage, as the provider measured it.

compute_seconds.description: Seconds of compute, when the provider counts them.

egress_bytes.description: Bytes sent out, when the provider says.

errors.description: Errors, when the provider counts them.

requests.description: Requests, when the provider counts them.

storage_bytes.description: Bytes stored, when the provider says.

VariableAddress.description:
One address a variable points at, as far as it shows where, never what
it holds: `DATABASE_URL` → `aws-0-eu-west-3.pooler.supabase.com`, user
`postgres.abcd`.

host.description: The host name in the address.

user.description: The user name in the address, when it has one.

Webhook.description: Where a background agent hears about what happens in Hoista.

events.description:
Event kinds it gets, such as `deploy.succeeded`, or a family ending in
`.*` such as `deploy.*`. Empty means every kind.

project_id.description: Only this project's events, when set.

WebhookDelivery.description: One event sent, or to be sent, to one webhook.

last_error.description: Why the last try didn't work, in plain words.

last_status.description: The receiver's last HTTP status, if it answered.

next_attempt_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC: the next try, while pending.
